group_assessment.weighting: A paediatric neurology and metabolic-genetics group (Prince Sultan Military Medical City, from the affiliations) that sees WWOX-null children. Primary for the clinical phenotype of biallelic loss (it adds an unpublished sibling family); not a mechanism group. Its clinical restatements weigh as a summary of cited reports; its mechanism paragraph weighs as speculation.

entries.proposition: A second human biallelic nonsense case is described as a 'virtual full knockout'; the commentary cites no RNA or protein study showing absence of WWOX in that family.
entries.snippet: In this case, the homozygous WWOX germline alteration is a nonsense mutation at arginine 54 (pArg54*) leading to a virtual WWOX human full knockout case.
entries.anchor: Mutation in WWOX gene cause microcephaly, growth retardation, epilepsy, retinal degeneration, and early death

entries.proposition: The commentary says the clinical series confirm each other and resemble the lde/lde rat, a rat whose allele the same commentary describes, earlier, as a 13-base-pair deletion that frameshifts the last 44 codons (so 'functional null' is the commentary's characterisation of a C-terminal frameshift).
entries.snippet: These two reports confirm the observation of Mallaret et al.,8 but in more severe phenotype, and are highly similar to the abnormalities reported in lde/lde rats with a spontaneous functional null mutation of WWOX, expanding the nervous system clinical presentation of WWOX gene mutation.
